column1: # Root senses. Columns: root, plain English sense, French.
# Each sense was written from the root's own words in the bundled corpus — their
# glosses and their occurrence counts — and then tested rather than trusted:
# server/cmd/rootcheck scores a proposal against the root's glosses in every
# morphological shape, measures the share of the root's occurrences it explains,
# holds every word of it either to what the root attests or to the company the
# corpus keeps it in, asks whether any one branch of the root is left unnamed,
# and asks whether the clause a reader reads first is the branch they are
# likeliest to meet. A sense that fails ships nothing, and a row with no French
# is a row that failed: French is translated from the English that passed and is
# never written independently, because the corpus carries no French gloss to
# A root the Qur'an realises in more than one branch names them all, heaviest
# first, because a sense that explains a minority of its own occurrences leaves
# the word a reader actually meets unexplained and a sense that names the
# minority first tells them the wrong thing before they read on: غير is met as
# غَيْر, "other than", far more often than as "to change", نفق as مُنَافِقُون far
# more often than as spending, and they say so, in that order. The order is not
# taste: "rootcheck order <tsv>" sorts each row's clauses by how many of the
# root's occurrences each one explains, and moves the French with the English.
# Where the corpus cannot tell two roots apart — where its glosses for both are
# the same English words — both ship nothing, and the few rows commented out
# below say which root the prose was left to and why.
# Nothing here is quoted from or attributed to any lexicon or scholar. Nothing
# here is a claim about a verse.
